simple.meaning: עָדַן (ʻâdan) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to be soft or pleasant ; figuratively and reflexively, to live voluptuously.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Nehemiah, beginning at Nehemiah 9:25. The surrounding contexts include land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עָדַן (H5727) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: עָדַן (ʻâdan) / H5727 is traced through Nehemiah 9:25 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to be soft or pleasant ; figuratively and reflexively, to live voluptuously
definitions.full: H5727. adan [ עָדַן ] verb denominative Hithpa`el luxuriate (Late Hebrew Pi`el delight (active), so Syriac ; — Imperfect 3masculine plural בְּטוּבְךָ וַיִּתְעַדְּנוּ Neh 9:25 and they luxuriated in thy great goodness (+ וַיַּשְׁמִינוּ וַיִּשְׂבְּעוּ וַיּאֹכְלוּ ).

occurrences.englishText: They took fortified cities and a rich land, and possessed houses full of all good things, cisterns dug out, vineyards, olive groves, and fruit trees in abundance. So they ate, were filled, became fat, and delighted themselves in your great goodness.
